body:
### Suggestion
In my opinion, we should add links or include at least one code example in the control itself. I understand that it might be difficult to provide examples for every programming language, but we could use pseudocode or a general example instead.
For first control : 
<html>
<body>
<!--StartFragment-->
1.1.1 | Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further, for example it is not performed after input validation or sanitization.

<!--EndFragment-->
</body>
</html>


### Code example
```
`def insecure(user_input):
#step 1 : Validate user input
if '..' in user_input:
   Exception("Blocked")
#step 2 : Decode after validation (bad)! 
decoded_input = decode_input(user_input)
open(decoded_input)

if I pass this input  to insecure method %2e%2e%2fetc%2fpasswd, then it will pass the validation and after decoding the input become '../etc/passwd'

Boom : Path traversal occurs
```

I think by giving example we can make it easy. I am happy to volunteer and add example where ever possible. 
Thanks

comments.body:
Hi,

This is something that can be built on top of ASVS requirements - part of the testing guide, implementation guide, or just extra educational and learning material. 

Some background information - the intent for ASVS requirements at the moment is "pure requirements only".

First, we don't have the time and resources to handle an extra layer on top of requirements - to have pseudo-code examples or just examples for ~350 requirements is worth a separate project already.

Second, we don't want any content other than requirements to be part of "releasable content". Otherwise, making a change in a code example requires a new release. In this case, it could be confusing for ASVS users because the requirement did not change. So we want to be really stable with releases.

In general, all these extra layers that can be built on top of ASVS, we will watch after the release of v5.0 (expected to happen at the end of this month). Meanwhile, ideas and visions can be collected.
